_comment: Selection happens at RESOLUTION time (release notes: 'you must choose and banish ... when the triggered effect resolves'), so there is no ability-level target; MOVE_MATCHING is the selector because it is the only arena-scoped primitive that chooses AND records its choice (record_as) - LOOK_AT only scans DECK_TOP/ARSENAL/HAND and plain BANISH cannot leave the arena. Steps follow the printed order: banish to the OWNER's banished zone (MOVE_MATCHING destinations default to obj.owner), return to the owner's permanents (auras live in player.permanents - Player.auras is a SubZoneView over it - hence zone name 'permanents'), THEN put the holo counter. That last ordering is load-bearing: Zone.add calls reset_to_base_state() when a card leaves the arena (CR 3.0.9; state.py ~252, card.py:480 clears card.counters), so an earlier draft that put the counter on BEFORE the banish-round-trip shipped an aura that came back with no holo counter. NOT/HAS_COUNTER compiles via the flattened inner_type form (condition_types.py:2220); triage's 'CARD_TYPE_IN' does not exist - CARD_IS_TYPE is the real condition and checks types AND subtypes, which is what 'Aura' needs (all 35 Lightning auras in card data carry subtype Aura + talent Lightning). Release-note 'no priority between any of the effects' holds: all three steps run inside one ability resolution. KNOWN GAP, flagged: if you control no qualifying aura at resolution, MOVE_MATCHING finds nothing and the whole ability fizzles silently; the printed card is effectively unplayable in that spot rather than fizzle-y, and play-time targeting is not enforced on this path.
